//catalog-growth-correction: CORRECTION (issue #674). Several notes below justify a budget bump with the claim that adding copy to the root next-intl catalog 'lands in the shared chunk and so costs every route about 1 kB'. That claim is wrong and should not be reused as precedent. It was first written in //media-picker, then cited by //multi-creator; //planner-serving-allocations rests on the same reasoning. Message catalogs do not contribute to First Load JS. Evidence: (1) a production build was searched for distinctive strings from three namespaces (mediaPicker, pwa, common) -- zero matches in .next/static/**/*.js, matches only in .next/server/chunks/*.js, because src/app/layout.tsx passes messages to NextIntlClientProvider as a prop, so they are serialized into the per-request RSC flight payload rather than compiled into a client chunk; (2) the / route is a clean control -- it renders no image field and no co-creator UI, and it has not moved (224.0 kB on a local Windows build) across both the mediaPicker and the recipeCreators catalog additions, though the claim predicts +1 kB for each. What actually moved those routes was code, not copy: the ~1 kB was ImageUploadField / media-picker-config wiring, which per-route module analysis found on exactly the three routes that grew and absent from /. The budget numbers below are NOT changed by this correction -- they were re-baselined to values that the measured routes genuinely need, so the limits are sound even though the stated reasoning was not. Only the diagnosis is corrected. The real cost of catalog growth is RSC payload transfer and hydration, which this gate does not measure at all; per-route message scoping is tracked in #674. Note the constraint any such change faces: use-intl's IntlProvider replaces messages on nesting rather than merging them, so a nested provider carrying only route namespaces would drop the globals. Before bumping a budget for 'catalog growth' again, measure which modules entered the route.

Hash equality is the stronger form, because it also rules out compensating changes that a kB total would hide. The mid-branch Linux failure (254.0 vs 253) was real but TRANSIENT: the branch's final pre-merge run measured 253.0, which passes the original 253 budget under `actual <= budget` (check-bundle-budget.mjs:70). Note that is a claim about what would have turned CI red, not about actual bytes: next build prints First Load JS as integers at this magnitude, so the true size could be 253.4 and still print 253 -- but the gate only ever compares the printed number. So the 253 -> 255 bump was not load-bearing at merge -- BUT KEEP IT. /recipes still measures 253.0 on Linux, so reverting restores a zero-headroom budget, and zero headroom is the underlying fault this whole correction is about. No replacement cause is offered for the transient kB because none was established; do not substitute one.
